In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a highly pathogenic avian influenza A virus from an avirulent field isolate by passaging in chickens.
the generation of a highly virulent avian flu virus from an avirulent field isolate by passaging in chickens.
the generation of highly pathogenic influenza A viruses (HPAIV) from avirulent wild-type influenza A viruses (WTIAV).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the generation of a highly virulent avian virus from avirulent wild waterfowl virus is possible, and this mechanism is likely to be the source of the H5N1 virus outbreaks in poultry in Southeast Asia.
highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) can arise from avian influenza viruses in wild waterfowls.

highly pathogenic avian influenza virus (HPAIV) could be generated from a benign wild bird influenza virus by serial passage in chickens, but the mechanism by which this occurs has not been determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus can arise from avian influenza virus in wild waterfoul by passaging in chickens, and this is the first report that highly pathogenic avain influenza virus can arise in wild waterfouls.

a highly pathogenic avian influenza virus was generated from an avirulent field isolate by passage in chickens, which suggests that wild waterfowl may be a natural reservoir of avian influenza viruses that have the potential to acquire the highly pathogenic phenotype in domestic poultry.
the avian influenza A virus (H5N1) can be generated from an avirulent strain in wild birds, and that the virus is able to infect and kill chickens, which are the main source of the virus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) are capable of emerging from avirulent wild-type strains.
highly virulent viruses can arise from viruses in wild bird populations, and that the mechanism of acquisition of virulence is the same in both poultry and wild birds.
avirulent influenza viruses circulating in wild birds can acquire virulence during passage in poultry.
